"""
Project Title: Neural Relational Inference for Physical Dynamics (ai-ml-ds-NRIPhysics2025)
File Name: neural_relational_inference_physics.py

Short Description:
Implements a Neural Relational Inference (NRI) model in Keras to learn both the underlying interaction graph 
and the dynamics of a multi‐particle spring system from trajectories. Uses an encoder to infer edges,
a graph neural network to predict future velocities, and a decoder to reconstruct positions.

"""

import os  # type: ignore
import numpy as np  # type: ignore
import tensorflow as tf  # type: ignore
from tensorflow.keras import layers, Model, Input  # type: ignore

# ============================
# 1. Hyperparameters & Setup
# ============================
SEED: int = 42
np.random.seed(SEED); tf.random.set_seed(SEED)
N_PARTICLES: int = 5         # type: int = number of nodes
DIM: int = 2                 # type: int = coordinate dimension
ENC_HIDDEN: int = 128        # type: int = encoder MLP size
DEC_HIDDEN: int = 128        # type: int = decoder MLP size
EDGE_TYPES: int = 2          # type: int = types of interactions (spring/no‐spring)
SEQ_LEN: int = 50            # type: int = input sequence length
PRED_STEPS: int = 10         # type: int = predict this many future steps
LR: float = 1e-3             # type: float = learning rate
BATCH_SIZE: int = 32         # type: int = batch size
EPOCHS: int = 200            # type: int = training epochs
LOG_DIR: str = "./nri_logs"
os.makedirs(LOG_DIR, exist_ok=True)

# ===================================
# 2. Synthetic Spring‐Mass Trajectories
# ===================================
def generate_spring_data(batch_size: int = BATCH_SIZE) -> tuple:
    """
    Generates batch of synthetic trajectories of N_PARTICLES connected by random springs.
    Returns:
      pos_seq: (batch, SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM)
      vel_seq: (batch, SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM)
    """
    pos_seq = np.zeros((batch_size, SEQ_LEN+PRED_STEPS, N_PARTICLES, DIM), dtype="float32")
    vel_seq = np.zeros_like(pos_seq)
    for b in range(batch_size):
        # random initial positions/velocities
        pos = np.random.randn(N_PARTICLES, DIM)
        vel = np.random.randn(N_PARTICLES, DIM)*0.1
        # random adjacency
        adj = (np.random.rand(N_PARTICLES,N_PARTICLES) < 0.5).astype("float32")
        adj = np.triu(adj,1); adj += adj.T
        k = 0.1  # spring constant
        for t in range(SEQ_LEN+PRED_STEPS):
            # simple Euler integration
            forces = np.zeros((N_PARTICLES,DIM),dtype="float32")
            for i in range(N_PARTICLES):
                for j in range(N_PARTICLES):
                    if adj[i,j]:
                        diff = pos[j]-pos[i]
                        forces[i] += k * diff
            vel = vel + forces * 0.01
            pos = pos + vel * 0.01
            pos_seq[b,t] = pos
            vel_seq[b,t] = vel
    # split into encoder input and decoder target
    return pos_seq[:,:SEQ_LEN], vel_seq[:,:SEQ_LEN], pos_seq[:,SEQ_LEN:], vel_seq[:,SEQ_LEN:]

# ============================
# 3. Encoder: Edge Inference
# ============================
# Input: concatenated positions & velocities over SEQ_LEN
enc_in = Input((SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM*2), name="enc_in")
# Aggregate over time via 1D conv
x = layers.TimeDistributed(layers.Dense(ENC_HIDDEN, activation="relu"))(enc_in)
x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling1D()(x)   # shape (batch, N_PARTICLES, ENC_HIDDEN)
# For each pair i,j, compute edge logits
# repeat and concat for pairs
h_i = layers.Lambda(lambda z: tf.repeat(z[:, :, None, :], N_PARTICLES, axis=2))(x)
h_j = layers.Lambda(lambda z: tf.repeat(z[:, None, :, :], N_PARTICLES, axis=1))(x)
h_ij = layers.Concatenate()([h_i, h_j])  # (batch, N, N, 2*ENC_HIDDEN)
edge_logits = layers.Dense(EDGE_TYPES, activation="softmax", name="edge_logits")(h_ij)
encoder = Model(enc_in, edge_logits, name="encoder")

# ============================
# 4. Decoder: Graph Neural Dynamics
# ============================
# Inputs: last positions, last velocities, and inferred edges
pos_in = Input((N_PARTICLES, DIM), name="pos_in")
vel_in = Input((N_PARTICLES, DIM), name="vel_in")
edges_in = Input((N_PARTICLES, N_PARTICLES, EDGE_TYPES), name="edges_in")
# message passing per edge type
msgs = []
for et in range(EDGE_TYPES):
    e_ij = layers.Lambda(lambda z: z[:,:,:,et:et+1])(edges_in)
    # compute messages: (pos_i, pos_j, vel_i, vel_j)
    h_i = layers.Concatenate()([pos_in, vel_in])
    h_j = h_i
    h_ij = layers.Concatenate(axis=-1)([layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.repeat(x[:,:,None,:],N_PARTICLES,axis=2))(h_i),
                                         layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.repeat(x[:,None,:,:],N_PARTICLES,axis=1))(h_j)])
    m = layers.Dense(DEC_HIDDEN, activation="relu")(h_ij)
    # weight by edge probability
    m = layers.Multiply()([m, e_ij])
    # aggregate messages per node
    m_ag = tf.reduce_sum(m, axis=2)
    msgs.append(m_ag)
# sum over edge types
agg = layers.Add()(msgs)
# update via MLP
h = layers.Concatenate()([pos_in, vel_in, agg])
h = layers.Dense(DEC_HIDDEN, activation="relu")(h)
dv = layers.Dense(DIM, name="dv")(h)
# predict next velocity & position
vel_next = layers.Add()([vel_in, dv])
pos_next = layers.Add()([pos_in, vel_next])
decoder = Model([pos_in, vel_in, edges_in], [pos_next, vel_next], name="decoder")

# ============================
# 5. Full NRI Model & Training
# ============================
# Build autoencoder-like model
pos_seq_in = Input((SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM), name="pos_seq")
vel_seq_in = Input((SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM), name="vel_seq")
# prepare encoder input
enc_seq = layers.Concatenate(axis=-1)([pos_seq_in, vel_seq_in])  # shape (batch,SEQ,N,P,2D)
enc_flat = layers.Permute((1,3,2,4))(enc_seq)  # flatten N,D together
enc_flat = layers.Reshape((SEQ_LEN, N_PARTICLES, DIM*2))(enc_seq)
edges = encoder(enc_flat)  # (batch,N,N,EDGE_TYPES)
# iterate decoder for PRED_STEPS
pos = pos_seq_in[:,-1]
vel = vel_seq_in[:,-1]
pred_pos = []; pred_vel = []
for _ in range(PRED_STEPS):
    pos, vel = decoder([pos, vel, edges])
    pred_pos.append(pos); pred_vel.append(vel)
pred_pos = layers.Stack()(pred_pos)  # (batch,PRED,N,D)
# compile
model = Model([pos_seq_in, vel_seq_in], pred_pos, name="nri_model")
model.compile(optimizer=tf.keras.optimizers.Adam(LR),
              loss="mse")
# Training loop
for epoch in range(1, EPOCHS+1):
    P, V, Tpos, Tvel = generate_spring_data()
    loss = model.train_on_batch([P, V], Tpos)
    if epoch % 10 == 0:
        print(f"Epoch {epoch}/{EPOCHS} - Loss: {loss:.4f}")

# ============================
# 6. Example Use Cases
# ============================
# Use case: predict next positions for a new batch
P, V, Tpos, _ = generate_spring_data(4)
pred = model.predict([P, V])
print("Example prediction shape:", pred.shape)
print("True next pos (first sample):", Tpos[0,0])
print("Predicted next pos (first sample):", pred[0,0])

# ============================
# End of code
# ============================

Key Learnings & Research Areas:

  • Neural Relational Inference (NRI): unsupervised discovery of interaction graph and dynamics.
  • Graph Neural Networks: message passing conditioned on inferred edge types.
  • Applications: physical system identification, multi-agent modeling, molecular dynamics.

This project pushes Keras into joint graph‐structure learning and dynamical forecasting—state‐of‐the‐art meta‐modeling of interactions.
